name: astrocam
position_index_notes: Which physical camera/lens generation is installed. INCREMENT whenever the camera, lens or mounting is changed — each index is a distinct calibration epoch (plate scale, pole, FOV, orientation, pedestal) that must NOT be mixed across the boundary. Stamped into every FITS as POSINDEX so each frame self-identifies its epoch regardless of config drift. Registry below.

1.label: av2
1.notes: Original v2. Fixed-lens (twist-focus). Downstream 180 rotation via rotate_180=true. pedestal 512, plate_scale 0.0190, pole_prior [1945,1823].

2.label: av3s
2.notes: v3 standard swap. Software focus lp=1.0 (dithered 0.5-1.5). 180 rotation IN-CAPTURE (rotate_180=false). pedestal 105. plate_scale/pole/occlusion from v2 are STALE and must be re-solved.

3.label: av3sw
3.camera: Pi Camera Module v3 (standard) + tempered-glass window
3.notes: SAME imx708 module as epoch 2. Two changes make this a new epoch: (a) the camera was RETRACTED AND REMOUNTED, so pole position and rotation shift — pole_prior/plate_scale must be re-solved (they were already STALE from the v2 era, so nothing good was lost at this boundary); (b) a tempered-glass phone screen protector was fitted over the lens aperture for rain protection, i.e. a PERMANENT flat glass element in the optical path. Optics: plane-parallel plate in a collimated beam, so NO focus shift — lp=1.0 still stands, do not re-probe focus. Cost: ~8% transmission (uncoated, ~4%/surface) = ~0.12 stops on the log2(mean/pedestal) brightness chart and ~0.09 mag on limiting magnitude; possible ghosting on bright sources (Moon, streetlights). THE BRIGHTNESS SERIES STEPS DOWN AT THIS BOUNDARY AND THAT STEP IS THE GLASS, NOT A CALIBRATION BUG — same trap class as the stale 512 pedestal. pedestal 50 unchanged. Enclosure unchanged: the camera body itself seals the aperture, so the box was already sealed and the glass adds no thermal change (ΔT stayed ~25-27°C above ambient across the change). BOUNDARY 2026-08-20, AFFIRMED BY PETER. Note for anyone re-deriving it from the images: POINTING CANNOT DATE THIS BOUNDARY, because THE CAMERA IS CLAMPED. Phase-correlating the 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-20 max-stacks gives only 2 px at half-res (~4 px native = 0.057 deg = 3.4 arcmin; foreground-only dy=-2 dx=0, peak/sigma 14-25) — the clamp returns the camera to within a few px after being taken in, so a near-zero shift is EXPECTED across a remount and is NOT evidence the camera stayed put. USEFUL COROLLARY: the geometric half of this epoch break is small — epoch 3 pointing matches epoch 2 to ~3.4 arcmin, so the epoch-2 pole/plate solution is a good starting point rather than a write-off. THE REAL BREAK IS PHOTOMETRIC: the glass. NB the night of 2026-08-20 stacked only 96/465 (vs 210-340 on prior nights) — that is WEATHER, not the move: sky ran bright and swinging (per-hour mean 132-282 vs a steady 96-166 on 08-19), and variability is what defeats the stacker. BACKFILL OUTSTANDING: the 465 frames of the 2026-08-20 night were captured under epoch 3 but stamped POSINDEX=2 (config was bumped the following morning) — they need re-stamping to 3.

capture.lens_position_notes: imx708 manual focus in DIOPTRES. STELLAR best = ~1.4, confirmed 2026-07-30 by reading Night-1 star trails directly (lp~1.4 gives a tight sidereal streak; low end 0.5 is a defocus blob). The 2026-07-29 daytime-tree probe suggested ~1.0 but trees are finite-distance and focus lower than infinity — stars settled the value. Very different from eclipticam-v3w's 3.15 because that is the WIDE lens. Focus breathing minimal. Night daemon dithers tightly around 1.4 for per-frame refinement (LENSPOS header).
capture.focus_dither_notes: Tightened 2026-07-30 to 1.3-1.6/0.02 (16 positions) after reading Night-1 star trails directly: LENSPOS ~1.4 is sharply focused (tight sidereal trail), the low end (0.5) is a fat defocus blob — focus improves steadily UP the ramp. So STELLAR infinity is ~1.4 (NOT the daytime tree peak of 1.0-1.4 read finer, and NOT the low FWHM my crude script wrongly reported — that grabbed faint moving sources). Dense 0.02 step brackets 1.4 tightly to pin the exact optimum + give super-res focus data. If a night confirms a stable best, consider pinning fixed like eclipticam-v3w. NB astrocam is the STANDARD v3 (~4.74mm, ~66deg FOV) so its plate scale is ~1.7x finer than eclipticam's WIDE v3w — a star spans ~1.7x more px here, so compare PSF in arcsec (via plate scale) not raw px.
capture.capture_notes: Streaming single-frame-per-FITS via astro.capture.streaming (same engine as eclipticam-v3w), NOT the old imx219 short-exposure x8-coadd loop. 59.9s @ gain 1 matches eclipticam-v3w night params on the same sensor. RECALIBRATE from real imx708 sky frames: pole_prior_xy, plate_scale, pedestal, and occlusion tile map are all STALE (imx219 / v2-lens / 3280x2464 era).

plate_scale_notes: STALE (imx219/v2-lens era). Nominal Camera Module v2 stock lens, 62.2 deg / 3280 px. INVALID for the imx708 standard-v3 swap (2026-07-29): different lens FOV and 4608x2592 native. Must be re-solved from imx708 sky frames.
pole_prior_notes: STALE (imx219/3280x2464 coords). INVALID after the imx708 swap 2026-07-29 (native 4608x2592, different lens/FOV/mount alignment). Re-derive from imx708 sky frames before trusting.
rotate_180_notes: DOWNSTREAM rotation OFF as of the imx708 swap (2026-07-30). The imx708 streaming capture engine already rotates 180 in-capture (StreamingConfig rotation_180=True, Bayer [::-1,::-1]), matching eclipticam-v3w (whose rotate_180 is also unset). Under the OLD imx219 loop capture did NO rotation and the processing stage rotated via this flag (was true). Leaving it true after the swap DOUBLE-rotated (capture + processing = 360), inverting the sky — Polaris appeared above the pole instead of below. One rotation only: in capture.
pedestal_notes: CHART FLOOR ONLY — see black_level for the sensor's electronic zero and blackest_observed for the darkest sky actually recorded. Reference for the brightness chart's log2(mean/pedestal) 'stops' axis. Set to 50 on 2026-08-01 to guarantee >=1 STOP OF WINTER FOOTROOM: the darkest observed CLEAR summer sky (2026-07-31 02:10->dawn) had frame-mean 100.5, and winter clear nights will go darker still (longer/colder/less glow). pedestal=50 makes today's darkest sky read ~1.0 stop (log2(100.5/50)=1.01) and lets a further full stop of winter darkening (down to mean ~50) land before the chart floors at 0. NB this is BELOW the sensor's true per-pixel black level (~62-64) — so the axis is a DELIBERATE low reference for footroom, NOT a physical black-level measurement; chart shapes + clear/cloudy discrimination are unchanged, just shifted up ~1 stop from the old 99. History: was imx219's 512; imx708 first-night 105; lowered to 99 when the clear-sky floor turned out to be 100.5 (105 was flooring); now 50 for winter footroom.
black_level_notes: IMX708 sensor electronic zero: what a photosite reads with NO photons, in 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU. This is a physical property of the silicon — do NOT set it for convenience, that is what `pedestal` is for. CONFIDENCE: INFERRED, not measured. The nominal 64 is the documented IMX708 black level and is consistent with the earliest eclipticam v3w floor (64.82, an upper bound since it includes minimum sky). It has NOT been measured from true dark frames. To measure it properly: cap the lens and take a master dark — that is the only way to separate black level from the sky floor, and it also settles whether it moves with analog gain (asserted 2026-08-20 to stay at ~64 across gain, but that claim rested on a retracted premise and was never tested). NB the well-measured 64.073 figure is IMX219, NOT this sensor — see the position_registry v2 entry.
blackest_observed_notes: Darkest frame mean ever recorded on this camera+sensor, 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU, 2026-08-20, over n=9153 frames (mode imx708_streaming, from 2026-07-29). It is black_level + the minimum REAL sky signal, so FOOTROOM = blackest_observed - black_level = ~19.8 ADU of irreducible urban sky glow. Caveats: (1) a min-of-N estimator, biased low as frames accumulate, so it only ever falls and is not comparable across cameras with different N (eclipticam has ~2x the frames); (2) astrocam's early imx708 nights overlap its own commissioning, so pre-2026-08-04 values are not clean sky. Refresh from the quality DB, do not hand-edit downward.
frames_root_notes: Where this stream's frames live, the single source of truth (CameraConfig.frames_root). Resolved PER-HOST: the same physical store (muppet's bigstore, Seagate USB /mnt/bigstore/astro-data, NFS-exported ~2026-07-30) is reached by different paths on different machines, so one string can't be right everywhere. Default `frames_root` (~/astrocam-frames) is the capture Pi's view, where the export is NFS-automounted at that home path. `frames_root_by_host` overrides per short-hostname: on pip the same export is at /mnt/muppet/bigstore/astrocam-frames (pip's ~/astrocam-frames symlink was removed 2026-08-02). Add a host key to teach a new machine; capture+processing runs on the Pi (the default). NOT the old /mnt/bigdisk (frozen 2026-07-29).
night_layout_notes: YYYY-MM-DD/HH/MMSS.fits.fz (UTC dirs); night membership decided by DATE-OBS within the noon-rollover window.
sky_clear_max_stops_notes: Dark-trough (10-min anchor) stops above which the night is called cloudy. Set to 8.0 on 2026-08-03 after measuring the 5 imx708 nights 2026-07-29..08-02: on the pedestal-50 axis a CLEAR dark trough anchor reads 5.5-5.8 stops (NOT ~1 -- the ~1 in the old note was the darkest-single-window used for the chart y-axis, not the 10-min verdict anchor). The interim 5.0 cut straight through the clear-night population, so genuinely-clear dark nights 08-01/08-02 were mislabelled cloudy and lost their star-trail (max.jpg) + derot deliverables. 8.0 gives the worst clear night (5.81) a ~2.2-stop margin, matching the imx219-era clear/cloudy gap (threshold 4.0 sat ~2-3 stops above a just-under pedestal). Pedestal stays 50 deliberately (keeps the brightness chart usable with winter footroom); the cloud ceiling is decoupled from that choice by living on the same shifted axis. Re-derive if a fully-cloudy imx708 night shows the ceiling is too high.
state_notes: Night starts at sun -10 deg below horizon (ephem), matching eclipticam-v3w/v1 at the same site so all cameras transition together. Was the -12 default before 2026-06-20. sun_altitude_day_deg (-8) gives a small hysteresis band for astrocam-v3-gate (the sun-altitude service gate) so the boundary does not flap. NB: astro-state's brightness tier currently MISCLASSIFIES because the imx708 pedestal is STALE; the v3 night service is gated on sun altitude only (astrocam_v3_gate.py) until the pedestal is remeasured.
reference_nights_notes: Known dark/clear baseline overlaid on the combined-brightness chart (drawn coloured dashed). Same reference night as eclipticam-v3w. The latest night is drawn bold dashed black.
